```{r}
library(R.matlab)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
 
mat_path <- "Rutledge_GBE_risk_data_TOD.mat"
out_path <- "gbe_trials_full_R.csv.gz"
 
# --- Step 1: read the .mat file -------------------------------------------
m  <- readMat(mat_path)
sd <- m$subjData                       # struct array: one element per participant

# --- Step 0 (run these lines by hand once, then leave them commented) ------
# names(m)                             # should include "subjData" (and "depData")
# dim(sd)                              # field dimension first, then participants
# dimnames(sd)[[1]]                    # the 15 field names (id, age, ..., data)
# str(sd[[which(dimnames(sd)[[1]] == "age")]])   # peek at one value
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 
fields <- dimnames(sd)[[1]]
stopifnot(!is.null(fields), "data" %in% fields)
n <- length(sd) / length(fields)       # number of participants (expect 47067)
stopifnot(n == 47067)
 
# Flatten to a list-matrix: rows = fields, columns = participants.
S <- matrix(sd, nrow = length(fields), dimnames = list(fields, NULL))
 
num1 <- function(x) as.numeric(x)[1]   # first value of a scalar field
```
```{r}
# Pull every numeric matrix out of a nested list, however deeply it is wrapped
get_plays <- function(x) {
  if (is.matrix(x) && is.numeric(x)) return(list(x))
  if (is.list(x)) return(unlist(lapply(x, get_plays), recursive = FALSE))
  list()
}

# --- Step 2: build one small table per participant -------------------------
build_participant <- function(i) {
  plays <- get_plays(S[["data", i]])               # list of 30 x 15 matrices
  k     <- length(plays)
  stopifnot(k > 0, all(vapply(plays, nrow, integer(1)) == 30))
  X <- do.call(rbind, plays)                       # (30 * k) x 15

  # per-play values (timesPlayed, dayNumber, ...) padded/trimmed to k plays
  pad <- function(v) { v <- as.numeric(unlist(v)); length(v) <- k; v }
  per_play <- function(field) rep(pad(S[[field, i]]), each = 30)

  dev <- as.character(unlist(S[["deviceType", i]]))
  dev <- if (length(dev) == 0) NA_character_ else dev[1]

  tibble(
    participant_id    = num1(S[["id", i]]),
    play_index        = rep(seq_len(k), each = 30),
    play_number       = per_play("timesPlayed"),
    age_group         = num1(S[["age", i]]),
    is_female         = num1(S[["isFemale", i]]),
    location          = num1(S[["location", i]]),
    life_satisfaction = num1(S[["lifeSatisfaction", i]]),
    education         = num1(S[["education", i]]),
    native_language   = num1(S[["nativeLanguage", i]]),
    device_type       = dev,
    design_version    = per_play("designVersion"),
    day_number        = per_play("dayNumber"),
    time_of_day       = per_play("timeOfDay"),
    trial             = X[, 1],
    safe_value        = X[, 3],
    win_value         = X[, 4],
    lose_value        = X[, 5],
    chose_risky       = X[, 7],
    outcome           = X[, 8],
    choice_rt         = X[, 9],
    happiness         = X[, 10],
    happiness_start   = X[, 11],
    happiness_rt      = X[, 12]
  )
}

```

```{r}
one <- build_participant(1)
dim(one)                  # rows = 30 * plays, 23 columns at this stage
head(one)
system.time(test200 <- bind_rows(lapply(1:200, build_participant)))
nrow(test200)
```

```{r}
trials <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n), build_participant))
```


```{r}
trials <- trials %>%
  mutate(
    trial_type = case_when(safe_value > 0  ~ "gain",
                           safe_value == 0 ~ "mixed",
                           safe_value < 0  ~ "loss"),
    # 1 = gamble landed on the winning side, 0 = losing side, NA = safe choice
    won_gamble = if_else(chose_risky == 1, as.numeric(outcome == win_value), NA_real_),
    # result of the PREVIOUS trial; rows are ordered by trial within each play
    prev_chose = lag(chose_risky),
    prev_won   = lag(won_gamble),
    prev_result = case_when(
      trial == 1                      ~ NA_character_,
      prev_chose == 0                 ~ "safe",
      prev_chose == 1 & prev_won == 1 ~ "won",
      prev_chose == 1 & prev_won == 0 ~ "lost"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(participant_id, play_index, play_number, age_group, is_female, location,
         life_satisfaction, education, native_language, device_type,
         design_version, day_number, time_of_day, trial, trial_type,
         safe_value, win_value, lose_value, chose_risky, outcome, won_gamble,
         prev_result, choice_rt, happiness, happiness_start, happiness_rt) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ replace(.x, is.nan(.x), NA)))   # NaN -> NA
```

```{r}
# 01_load_and_check.R
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Loads the trial-level table made by python/convert_mat_to_csv.py and checks
# it against the published results (Rutledge et al., 2016; authors' .m script).
#
# STATUS: written without being able to run R, so it is UNTESTED in R. The
# expected values below were computed from the same table in Python.
#
# Setup:  install.packages(c("readr", "dplyr"))
#         Open the Assignment folder as an RStudio Project.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

trials <- read_csv("gbe_trials_full_R.csv.gz", show_col_types = FALSE)   # change the path if the file is elsewhere

# --- 1. Size checks ---------------------------------------------------------
cat("Rows:", nrow(trials), "(expect 2,731,740)\n")
cat("Participants:", n_distinct(trials$participant_id), "(expect 47,067)\n")
cat("Plays:", nrow(distinct(trials, participant_id, play_index)), "(expect 91,058)\n")
cat("Happiness ratings:", sum(!is.na(trials$happiness)), "(expect 1,092,696)\n")
stopifnot(nrow(trials) == 2731740, n_distinct(trials$participant_id) == 47067)

# --- 2. Age vs risk taking, FIRST play only (authors' .m script) -------------
age_cor <- function(type) {
  d <- trials %>%
    filter(play_index == 1, trial_type == type) %>%
    group_by(participant_id) %>%
    summarise(age = first(age_group), rate = mean(chose_risky), .groups = "drop")
  round(cor(d$age, d$rate), 3)
}
cat("Age vs gain gambling:  r =", age_cor("gain"),  "(expect about -0.11)\n")
cat("Age vs mixed gambling: r =", age_cor("mixed"), "(expect about  0.02)\n")
cat("Age vs loss gambling:  r =", age_cor("loss"),  "(expect about  0.00; not significant)\n")

# --- 3. Gamble rate by previous result (used by classroom mode) -------------
trials %>%
  filter(prev_result %in% c("won", "lost", "safe")) %>%
  group_by(prev_result) %>%
  summarise(n_trials = n(), gamble_rate = round(mean(chose_risky), 4)) %>%
  print()
# expect: lost 792,240 / 0.6749; safe 1,039,993 / 0.5010; won 808,449 / 0.6619
# Note: these pool all trial types. Gain/mixed/loss differ, so always split by trial_type.
```

Summary tables

After a loss minus after a win, by trial type: gain +0.0033, loss +0.0113 and mixed +0.0344. The person counts are 45,086, 45,101 and 42,705, and the confidence intervals match.
Gamble rate by trial type: gain 0.702, loss 0.536 and mixed 0.656, with 47,067 people each.
```{r}
# 02_summary_tables.R
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Builds the small summary tables the dashboard loads (instead of the raw
# 2.7M-row table). Method: compute each participant's own rate first, then
# average ACROSS PARTICIPANTS, so people who played many times do not count
# more and the confidence intervals reflect 47,067 people, not 2.7M trials.
#
# STATUS: UNTESTED in R. The same logic was run in Python; the expected
# results are in the comments and in the tables/ folder.
#
# Input : gbe_trials_full_R.csv.gz     Output: tables/*.csv
# age_group 0 means "all ages". low_n = TRUE when fewer than MIN_N people.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

trials <- read_csv("gbe_trials_full_R.csv.gz", show_col_types = FALSE)
dir.create("tables", showWarnings = FALSE)
MIN_N <- 30

# add an "all ages" copy (age_group = 0) to a participant-level table
with_all <- function(p) bind_rows(p, mutate(p, age_group = 0))

# mean, sd, se and 95% CI across participants for column `val`
summarise_people <- function(p, val, ...) {
  p %>%
    group_by(...) %>%
    summarise(n_participants = n(),
              mean = mean(.data[[val]]),
              sd   = sd(.data[[val]]),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(se      = sd / sqrt(n_participants),
           ci_low  = mean - qt(0.975, pmax(n_participants - 1, 1)) * se,
           ci_high = mean + qt(0.975, pmax(n_participants - 1, 1)) * se,
           low_n   = n_participants < MIN_N)
}

# --- Table 1: gamble rate by previous result --------------------------------
p1 <- trials %>%
  filter(prev_result %in% c("won", "lost", "safe")) %>%
  group_by(participant_id, age_group, trial_type, prev_result) %>%
  summarise(n_trials = n(), rate = mean(chose_risky), .groups = "drop")
p1a <- with_all(p1)

by_prev <- summarise_people(p1a, "rate", age_group, trial_type, prev_result) %>%
  rename(mean_rate = mean, sd_rate = sd, se_rate = se) %>%
  left_join(p1a %>% group_by(age_group, trial_type, prev_result) %>%
              summarise(n_trials = sum(n_trials), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("age_group", "trial_type", "prev_result"))
write_csv(by_prev, "tables/summary_by_previous_result.csv")

# --- Table 2: within-person difference, after a loss minus after a win ------
diffs <- p1 %>%
  filter(prev_result %in% c("won", "lost")) %>%
  select(participant_id, age_group, trial_type, prev_result, rate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = prev_result, values_from = rate) %>%
  filter(!is.na(won), !is.na(lost)) %>%          # need both cells for this person
  mutate(diff = lost - won)

lost_minus_won <- summarise_people(with_all(diffs), "diff", age_group, trial_type) %>%
  rename(mean_diff = mean, sd_diff = sd, se_diff = se)
write_csv(lost_minus_won, "tables/summary_lost_minus_won.csv")

# --- Table 3: gamble rate by age and trial type (lifespan view) -------------
p3 <- trials %>%
  group_by(participant_id, age_group, trial_type) %>%
  summarise(rate = mean(chose_risky), .groups = "drop")

age_trial <- summarise_people(with_all(p3), "rate", age_group, trial_type) %>%
  rename(mean_rate = mean, sd_rate = sd, se_rate = se)
write_csv(age_trial, "tables/summary_age_trial_type.csv")

# --- Checks (all ages; expected values from the Python run) ------------------
lost_minus_won %>% filter(age_group == 0) %>% print()
# expect mean_diff: gain 0.0033, loss 0.0113, mixed 0.0344 (n about 45,086 / 45,101 / 42,705)
age_trial %>% filter(age_group == 0) %>% print()
# expect mean_rate: gain 0.7016, loss 0.5361, mixed 0.6557 (n = 47,067)
```

The happiness table: mood after winning or getting nothing on gain and loss gambles, with the z-scoring from the authors’ script. This is needed for Daniel’s mood-to-choice view.

A trial-sequence table: one example participant’s choices and mood in order, for Daniel’s timeline view. This one is small.

```{r}
# 03_happiness_tables.R
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Happiness after outcomes, following the authors' MATLAB script
# (Rutledge_GBE_risk_data_code.m, section "Do expectations affect happiness").
# Their method, reproduced here:
#   * FIRST play of each participant only (data{1} in MATLAB)
#   * z-score each person's 12 ratings (mean and sd over that play)
#   * drop the rating made BEFORE trial 1
#   * give every trial the NEXT rating (so a rating is attached to the
#     trials leading up to it)
#   * keep trials where the person gambled; average z within person for:
#       gain_win  (gain trial, outcome > 0)   gain_zero (gain trial, got 0)
#       loss_zero (loss trial, got 0)         loss_loss (loss trial, outcome < 0)
#   * keep people who have all four cells
# Result: loss_zero is higher than gain_zero although both outcomes are 0,
# which is the "expectations affect happiness" finding.
#
# STATUS: UNTESTED in R. The same logic was run in Python and reproduced the
# published sample size exactly: n = 35,219.
# Input: gbe_trials_full_R.csv.gz     Output: tables/*.csv
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

trials <- read_csv("gbe_trials_full_R.csv.gz", show_col_types = FALSE)
dir.create("tables", showWarnings = FALSE)
MIN_N <- 30

with_all <- function(p) bind_rows(p, mutate(p, age_group = 0))
summarise_people <- function(p, val, ...) {
  p %>% group_by(...) %>%
    summarise(n_participants = n(), mean = mean(.data[[val]]), sd = sd(.data[[val]]), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(se = sd / sqrt(n_participants),
           ci_low  = mean - qt(0.975, pmax(n_participants - 1, 1)) * se,
           ci_high = mean + qt(0.975, pmax(n_participants - 1, 1)) * se,
           low_n = n_participants < MIN_N)
}

# --- 1. z-score within person and attach the NEXT rating to each trial ------
first_play <- trials %>%
  filter(play_index == 1) %>%
  arrange(participant_id, trial) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  mutate(rating_rank = cumsum(!is.na(happiness)),
         z = (happiness - mean(happiness, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(happiness, na.rm = TRUE),
         z = if_else(is.finite(z), z, NA_real_),             # constant ratings -> NA
         z_after = if_else(!is.na(happiness) & rating_rank > 1, z, NA_real_)) %>%
  fill(z_after, .direction = "up") %>%                       # take the next rating
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(happiness_z = z, happiness_z_filled = z_after)

# --- 2. mean z per person and outcome category ------------------------------
per_person <- first_play %>%
  filter(chose_risky == 1) %>%
  mutate(outcome_category = case_when(
    trial_type == "gain" & outcome > 0  ~ "gain_win",
    trial_type == "gain" & outcome == 0 ~ "gain_zero",
    trial_type == "loss" & outcome == 0 ~ "loss_zero",
    trial_type == "loss" & outcome < 0  ~ "loss_loss")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(outcome_category)) %>%
  group_by(participant_id, age_group, outcome_category) %>%
  summarise(z = mean(happiness_z_filled, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(z = if_else(is.finite(z), z, NA_real_)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = outcome_category, values_from = z) %>%
  drop_na(gain_win, gain_zero, loss_zero, loss_loss)          # people with all four cells

cat("Participants with all four cells:", nrow(per_person), "(expect 35,219)\n")
stopifnot(nrow(per_person) == 35219)

# --- Table 4: mean happiness (z) after each outcome -------------------------
outcomes_long <- per_person %>%
  pivot_longer(c(gain_win, gain_zero, loss_zero, loss_loss),
               names_to = "outcome_category", values_to = "z")
happy_out <- summarise_people(with_all(outcomes_long), "z", age_group, outcome_category) %>%
  rename(mean_z = mean, sd_z = sd, se_z = se)
write_csv(happy_out, "tables/summary_happiness_outcomes.csv")
happy_out %>% filter(age_group == 0) %>% print()
# expect mean_z: gain_win 0.342, gain_zero -0.157, loss_zero 0.120, loss_loss -0.386

# --- Table 5: the key comparison, loss_zero minus gain_zero ------------------
zero_diff <- per_person %>% mutate(diff = loss_zero - gain_zero)
happy_diff <- summarise_people(with_all(zero_diff), "diff", age_group) %>%
  rename(mean_diff = mean, sd_diff = sd, se_diff = se)
write_csv(happy_diff, "tables/summary_happiness_zero_diff.csv")
happy_diff %>% print()
# expect all ages: mean_diff 0.276, CI 0.268 to 0.285, n = 35,219

# --- Table 6: example choice/mood sequences for the timeline view ------------
# Deterministic subset (participant_id divisible by 250) so R and Python agree.
example_seq <- first_play %>%
  filter(participant_id %% 250 == 0) %>%
  select(participant_id, age_group, trial, trial_type, chose_risky, outcome,
         won_gamble, prev_result, happiness, happiness_z, happiness_z_filled)
write_csv(example_seq, "tables/example_sequences.csv")
cat("Example sequences:", n_distinct(example_seq$participant_id), "participants (expect 188)\n")
```
Getting nothing on a loss gamble means you avoided a loss. People report higher mood after getting zero in a loss gamble than after getting zero in a gain gamble, although the outcome is identical. The within-person gap is 0.28 (95% CI 0.27 to 0.29). It is the “expectations affect happiness” result from the original studies, and it holds in every age group.

New files

summary_happiness_outcomes.csv: mean mood by age group and outcome, with n and confidence intervals.
summary_happiness_zero_diff.csv: the within-person gap above, by age group.
example_sequences.csv: the first play of 188 participants, trial by trial, with their choices, outcomes, and mood (raw and z-scored). This is for Daniel’s timeline. I picked participants whose ID is divisible by 250, so the R and Python subsets are the same.
03_happiness_tables.R: the R script that makes all three.
